newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends tad weaker in arbitrage play.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends tad weaker in arbitrage play.

text.p: * Central Bank actively intervenes in the market
The Philippine peso slid slightly to 26.349 to the dollar at close from Thursday's 26.346 due to weekend arbitrage play, traders said.
"There's a lot of weekend play. Banks sold dollars valued today and bought them back valued Monday," one trader said.
Traders who bought dollars to be settled on Monday can hold on to their pesos and earn the relatively higher interest rate offered by the local currency during the weekend.
The Central Bank was active in the market, wedging the rates within a narrow range. It was bidding 26.341/26.343 valued today and 26.347/26.350 valued Monday.
"The players were squeezed by the small differentials between the Central Bank's bid-offer rates," one trader said.
The Central Bank was estimated to have bought about $50 million and sold about $100 million throughout the session.
Turnover was heavy with $282.3 million changing hands. Done rates were wedged between 26.34 and 26.35.
